as.bilingual_pair_policy: This Ghana Mathematics curriculum is English-only. Do not create bilingual pairs, translations, or cross-language duplicate candidates. Preserve visible English source text exactly. If non-English text appears incidentally, keep it only as source-visible text and do not translate it or pair it with an English candidate unless the document itself explicitly presents both versions as equivalent official curriculum text.

as.sfi_dedup_instructions:
Deduplicate Ghana Mathematics Basic 4–6 SFI candidates conservatively. Merge candidates only when they represent the same source-visible curriculum item. Same statement_type plus same normalized official code is strong merge evidence only when the descriptions/source_text are compatible and the source references are the same item, adjacent table-window overlap, or a clear continuation duplicate. Do not treat Ghana official codes as globally unique identity keys: the source contains apparent code reuse, duplication, and numbering anomalies where the same Content Standard or Indicator code is attached to different mathematical statements. Same official code with materially different descriptions, incompatible source contexts, or different mathematical content should not be merged. Different source rows, segments, or windows are not by themselves a reason to keep candidates separate when the bounded evidence shows adjacent overlap, continuation repetition, duplicate extraction of one occurrence, or an exact document-specific duplicate family. When the bounded evidence shows they are distinct source-visible curriculum items, keep them separate as individual SFIs and preserve same-code/different-content audit evidence for manual review and disambiguated final IDs. Use conflict or needs_review for same-code candidates only when they appear to be competing or incompatible extractions of the same source-visible item, or when the bounded evidence is insufficient to decide whether they are distinct source items. Similar or identical text with different official codes usually represents distinct Ghana curriculum items and should be keep_separate unless the bounded evidence clearly shows duplicate extraction of the same source item. Treat malformed visible codes with spaces, punctuation, or OCR/source numbering issues cautiously: merge only when the intended official code and source item are clear; otherwise choose needs_review. For no-code Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand groupings, do not merge by label alone. BASIC 4, BASIC 5, and BASIC 6 are grade-scoped organizers; merge case/format variants of the same grade when statement_type=Grade and there is no direct visible evidence that they refer to different grade scopes, but keep different grades separate. Inherited source_context_labels alone should not block same-grade merges because they may be stale or noisy around divider pages, repeated heading blocks, or layout transitions. Strand and Sub-Strand labels such as Number Operations, Fractions, Measurement, Position/Transformation, Data, or repeated local numbers like Strand 1 and Sub-Strand 1 may recur under different grades or hierarchy contexts; merge only when the label, statement_type, and visible source context indicate the same organizer, otherwise keep_separate. Source-row/header overlap, same source segment, same window proximity, duplicate buckets, and same-code buckets are review signals only, not automatic merge rules.

Mixed-type duplicate-extraction correction:
- Do not keep candidates separate solely because their statement_type or normalized_statement_type differs.
- When candidates in the same bounded review set cite the same exact source occurrence, such as the same raw table row/header or the same source-visible heading, and their complete wording is identical or one candidate is a clearly bounded extraction of the other, treat the type difference as an extraction-classification disagreement. Merge them when the source role is clear and select canonical_type_source_candidate_id from the existing candidate whose type matches that source role.
- Use Ghana source role as the classification authority: a visible BASIC 4, BASIC 5, or BASIC 6 organizer is Grade; a visible Strand organizer is Strand; a visible Sub-Strand organizer is Sub-Strand; an official item in the CONTENT STANDARD(S) column with a four-component B4-B6 code or a clearly source-designated Content Standard role is Content Standard; and an official learning outcome in the INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS column with a five-component B4-B6 code or a clearly source-designated Indicator role is Indicator. A malformed or null code does not change a clear source-column role.
- Same-occurrence provenance and compatible complete wording are required. Do not merge genuinely different source items merely to reconcile their types.

Known Basic 4 fractions editorial anomaly:
- In the Basic 4 Fractions section, the Content Standard coded B4.1.3.1 with description "Develop an understanding of equivalent and improper fractions" is a legitimate distinct source item. Keep this candidate separate.
- Later continuation rows incorrectly print B4.1.3.1 beside the description "Demonstrate an understanding of strategies for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions (same denominator, or one being a multiple of the others)." The same description is subsequently introduced as B4.1.3.2. Treat the B4.1.3.1 occurrence with this comparison/addition/subtraction description as an editorially mislabelled occurrence of the B4.1.3.2 Content Standard.
- When these candidates occur in the same bounded review set: (1) keep the B4.1.3.1 equivalent/improper-fractions Content Standard separate; (2) merge the comparison/addition/subtraction candidate printed as B4.1.3.1 with the candidate printed as B4.1.3.2; (3) select the candidate printed as B4.1.3.2 as canonical_code_source_candidate_id for the mixed-code merge; (4) preserve both printed codes, source_text values, row provenance, and the source anomaly in the merge evidence; (5) do not rewrite either extraction candidate or silently replace its source-visible code; and (6) do not return conflict or needs_review for this exact known pattern.
- This document-specific rule overrides the general presumption that identical descriptions with different official codes normally remain separate.

Known Basic 4 Position/Transformation duplicated section:
- The source prints the same Position/Transformation organizer, Content Standard, Indicator, wording, examples, and diagram twice: first as "Sub-strand 2: Position / Transformation" with B4.3.2.1 and B4.3.2.1.1, and later as "Sub-strand 3: Position/Transformation" with B4.3.3.1 and B4.3.3.1.1.
- Treat the later Sub-strand 3 / B4.3.3.1 family as an editorially duplicated and misnumbered copy of the earlier Sub-strand 2 / B4.3.2.1 family, not as a separate logical curriculum branch.
- When the paired candidates occur in the same bounded review set, merge the two Sub-Strand occurrences, merge the two Content Standard occurrences, and merge the two Indicator occurrences. Preserve both printed labels, codes, source_text values, and provenance in the merge evidence.
- For the mixed-code Content Standard merge, select the B4.3.2.1 candidate as canonical_code_source_candidate_id. For the mixed-code Indicator merge, select the B4.3.2.1.1 candidate as canonical_code_source_candidate_id. Prefer the earlier "Sub-strand 2: Position / Transformation" candidate as representative for the grouping merge.
- This exact document-specific duplication overrides the general presumption that identical wording with different official codes remains separate.

Known Basic 4 B4.3.3.1 collision boundary:
- The source also uses B4.3.3.1 and B4.3.3.1.1 for an earlier perimeter Content Standard and Indicator. Those perimeter statements are distinct from the later Position/Transformation statements printed with the same codes.
- When a bounded review set contains the perimeter candidates, the B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 Position/Transformation candidates, and the later B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1 Position/Transformation candidates, merge only the two Position/Transformation occurrences according to the duplicate-family rule. Keep the perimeter Content Standard and Indicator separate.
- Preserve same-code/different-content audit evidence between the final perimeter items and the later Position/Transformation source occurrences. Do not include the perimeter candidates in the mixed-code Position/Transformation merge.

Known B6.3.3.5 same-code/different-content case:
- Keep "Describe the position of objects in space using the cardinal points" separate from "Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection translation) on a 2D shape" even though both are printed as B6.3.3.5.
- Likewise keep their distinct B6.3.3.5.1 Indicator statements separate. Preserve the same-code/different-content audit evidence; do not select one statement as a correction of the other.

Known B5.3.2.2 same-code/different-content case:
- Keep "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape" separate from "Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes" even though both are printed as B5.3.2.2. They are distinct source-visible Content Standards, not continuation or duplicate-extraction variants.
- The transformation statement is part of an editorial parallel-column collision beside Algebra Indicators B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3. Do not merge it with those Indicators, with the volume Content Standard, or with any measurement continuation merely because of row proximity or the reused code.
- Preserve same-code/different-content audit evidence for the two B5.3.2.2 Content Standards. When the bounded evidence clearly contains these two descriptions, keep_separate rather than conflict or needs_review.

Known Basic 5 Geometry and Measurement grouping anomaly:
- The source-visible heading "Sub-strand 3: Measurement – Perimeter, Area, Capacity/Volume and Angle" is an editorial placement and numbering error. It appears while the source is still continuing the preceding Lines and Shapes material and does not establish a separate logical Measurement branch.
- The later heading "Sub-Strand 2: Measurement" introduces the actual Basic 5 Measurement sub-strand and is followed by source-visible measurement standards in the B5.3.2.x family. This does not include the anomalous transformation Content Standard also printed as B5.3.2.2 in the earlier parallel-column collision.
- When these two Sub-Strand candidates occur in the same bounded review set with Grade "BASIC 5" and Strand "Geometry and Measurement", merge them into one logical Sub-Strand. Use the candidate whose visible description is "Sub-Strand 2: Measurement" as representative_candidate_id, retain canonical statement value "Measurement", and preserve both source-visible headings and all provenance in the merged group.
- Do not keep the two candidates as separate singleton groups, because they have the same no-code semantic identity under this runtime configuration. Do not return conflict or needs_review for this exact known pattern.
- This is an exact document-specific exception. Do not generalize it into a rule that similarly named, same-value, or repeated no-code organizers should normally be merged.

Known Basic 5 stale B5.1.1.1 continuation occurrence:
- The genuine B5.1.1.1 Content Standard is the Basic 5 place-value standard introduced at the start of that family. A later row repeats B5.1.1.1 with a stale "up to 100,000 CONT'D" place-value description beside material from the later factors/even-and-odd-number sequence. That later occurrence is copied continuation residue, not a second logical Content Standard.
- When the genuine B5.1.1.1 candidate and the later stale continuation candidate occur in the same bounded review set, merge them into one Content Standard. Use the genuine introduced B5.1.1.1 candidate as representative_candidate_id and canonical_code_source_candidate_id. Preserve the stale printed wording, code anchor, row provenance, and anomaly in the merged evidence.
- Do not keep the stale continuation as a separate singleton and do not return conflict or needs_review for this exact known pattern.

Known Basic 5 anomalous B5.1.2.1.1 multiplication occurrence — source-faithful preservation policy:
- The source contains a genuine B5.1.2.1.1 Indicator in the Basic 5 Number Operations sequence and a separate row in the B5.1.4.1 decimal section that is also printed as B5.1.2.1.1 but says "Multiply multi-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers efficiently".
- Preserve the decimal-section multiplication occurrence as an independent source-visible Indicator. When it is reviewed with the genuine B5.1.2.1.1 Indicator, return keep_separate and preserve same-code/different-content audit evidence. Do not return conflict or needs_review merely because the printed code is clearly anomalous.
- Do not silently rewrite this occurrence to B5.1.2.2.1 and do not merge it with a B5.1.2.2.1 multiplication Indicator solely because the wording is identical or nearly identical. Under this runtime policy, the anomalous printed occurrence remains a separate audited SFI so the KG faithfully preserves the source PDF.
- This exact document-specific preservation rule overrides any general preference to correct obvious copied codes or merge semantically near-identical statements across different printed occurrences.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions:
Extract candidate StandardsFrameworkItems (SFIs) from the Ghana Mathematics curriculum only when the visible text is an official curriculum framework item or structural organizer within the target Basic 4–6 curriculum scope. Treat BASIC 4, BASIC 5, and BASIC 6 headings as Standard Grouping SFIs. Treat Strand headings and Sub-Strand headings as Standard Grouping SFIs when they are visible as curriculum organizers. When a single visible heading line or block contains both a Strand and a Sub-Strand, extract both source-visible organizers as separate Standard Grouping SFI candidates. Treat Content Standards with official Basic 4–6 codes such as B4.1.1.1, B5.1.1.1, or B6.1.1.1 as Standard SFIs. Treat Indicators with official Basic 4–6 codes such as B4.1.1.1.1, B5.1.1.1.1, or B6.1.1.1.1 as Standard SFIs. Do not extract KG1, KG2, B1, B2, or B3 codes, labels, sample rows, or annotation examples as SFI candidates when they appear in overview, organization, scope-and-sequence, annotation, or code-explanation sections. Those earlier-grade examples are explanatory context for the code system, not target Basic 4–6 curriculum items for this run. Do not extract LearningComponents in this step: do not decompose a content standard or indicator into smaller skills, concepts, lesson objectives, or teachable subskills. Treat exemplars, examples beginning with E.g., classroom activities, assessment suggestions, teacher guidance, resources, duration/time allocations, values, and pedagogical notes as non-SFI text. Do not emit routine auxiliary candidates for this material; use an auxiliary candidate only when source-visible text is genuinely ambiguous and likely to be mistaken for an SFI. Treat Subject Specific Practices and Core Competencies as non-SFI guidance and do not emit routine auxiliary candidates for them unless a document-specific profile explicitly overrides this policy. Repeated table headers and repeated continuation labels are not SFIs. Preserve source-language wording. The description must preserve the complete official Grade, Strand, Sub-Strand, Content Standard, or Indicator wording. For visible organizers, retain the hierarchy label, ordinal, punctuation, and topic together; for example, preserve "Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations" rather than shortening it to "Variables and Equations". Do not include a separately printed item code in description. Keep the formatting-normalized code in statement_code and preserve the exact raw code surface in the source_text evidence quote. A complete four- or five-component Basic 4–6 code that is printed immediately adjacent to statement text, or that differs only by spacing around periods or trailing punctuation, is formatting-recoverable and should be separated from the statement without changing any code character or numeric component. Thus "B5. 1.2.3.1 Determine basic division fact up to 81" uses statement_code="B5.1.2.3.1", and "B5.1. 4.1.3 Round decimals to the nearest tenth and hundredth" uses statement_code="B5.1.4.1.3", while source_text preserves each raw printed form. Use statement_code only when an official complete code is visible in the candidate's own source text. Preserve visibly malformed or incomplete source codes in source_text and keep statement_code null rather than repairing a prefix, adding a component, or changing a numeric component. Within one extraction result, repeated renderings of the same continued source item with the same statement type, normalized code, and complete description must produce one candidate with all contributing row indexes. This consolidation applies only to continuation copies or visible fragments of one logical source item. Independently printed duplicate sections and independently printed complete occurrences must remain separate extraction candidates even when their wording or codes match; downstream deduplication decides whether those physical occurrences represent one logical curriculum item. The same code with materially different descriptions must remain separate.

Known source-code collision boundaries
- B4.3.3.1 and B4.3.3.1.1 are used for an earlier perimeter Content Standard/Indicator and later for the duplicated Position/Transformation Content Standard/Indicator. Preserve the perimeter statements and the later Position/Transformation statements as separate extraction candidates. Do not combine them merely because their printed codes match. The later Position/Transformation occurrence also remains separate at extraction time from the independently printed B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 occurrence; downstream deduplication applies the exact duplicate-family rule.
- B5.3.2.2 is printed for both "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape" and "Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes". Preserve both as separate Content Standard candidates when visible. The transformation statement is an editorial column collision and must not be combined with the volume statement or with the neighboring Algebra Indicators.

Required semantic scope output
- Every SFI candidate must include both identity_scope_values and code_scope_values.
- Use these exact identity-scope shapes for this curriculum:
  - Grade: {}
  - Strand: {"Grade": one of "BASIC 4", "BASIC 5", or "BASIC 6"}
  - Sub-Strand: {"Grade": canonical Grade, "Strand": canonical Strand}
  - Content Standard: {"Grade": canonical Grade, "Strand": canonical Strand}
  - Indicator: {"Grade": canonical Grade, "Strand": canonical Strand}
- The only canonical Strand values are "Number", "Algebra", "Geometry and Measurement", and "Data". Use configured aliases only to recognize source wording; emit the canonical values in identity_scope_values.
- code_scope_statement_types is empty because the printed B4-B6 codes are document-global within this source. Therefore every candidate must emit code_scope_values={} whether coded or uncoded.
- Resolve Grade and Strand independently for each candidate occurrence. Explicit hierarchy labels in the candidate's own visible source units are strongest, followed by explicit hierarchy labels in the current visible heading block. When a required dimension remains absent, use the nearest compatible heading in the bounded section context; do not skip a nearer compatible value for an older one unless candidate-local visible source directly contradicts it. When a heading block visibly contains both a Strand and a Sub-Strand, the Sub-Strand candidate uses the Strand from that same block rather than an older inherited section label.
- Do not select hierarchy scope from incidental vocabulary inside Content Standards, Indicators, exemplars, activities, resources, competencies, notes, calculations, or neighboring parallel columns. Words such as number, data, measurement, shape, or algebra inside ordinary curriculum prose are not scope evidence by themselves. Do not assign one shared Strand merely because different candidates occupy the same table row or window.
- Preserve surprising source placement and code inconsistencies. A printed code may support review or expose a conflict, but it must not silently replace a visibly active Grade or Strand heading. When candidate-local source role, exact code evidence, wording, and table geometry jointly conflict with the nearest heading, treat the case as a source-layout conflict and apply the document-specific rule below rather than automatically copying the heading. Record the conflict in extraction_notes when useful.
- Known source-layout conflict: one row places Content Standard B5.3.2.2, "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape", in the Content Standards column beside Algebra Indicators B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3 in the parallel Indicators column. Treat this as an editorial column collision. Assign B5.3.2.2 to Grade "BASIC 5" and Strand "Geometry and Measurement". Keep B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3 under Grade "BASIC 5" and Strand "Algebra". Same-row placement and the surrounding Algebra section must not force these separate column items into one shared Strand.
- Scope fields are semantic metadata, not additional SFI candidates. Do not invent a missing Strand or Sub-Strand organizer merely to populate scope.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions:
Validate Ghana Mathematics Basic 4-6 SFI extraction conservatively and source-faithfully. Apply the following curriculum-specific rules in addition to the generic checker rules and the extraction instructions.

1. Target scope and non-target sections
- The target SFIs are the official Basic 4, Basic 5, and Basic 6 hierarchy and statements in the detailed standards section: visible Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand organizers; coded Content Standards; and coded or clearly source-designated Indicators.
- Reject SFI candidates drawn from the cover, publication details, foreword, table of contents, rationale, philosophy, general or subject aims, instructional expectations, core competencies, learning domains, skills and processes, attitudes, values, assessment, time allocation, pedagogy, inclusion, differentiation, ICT guidance, panel-member lists, and other front or back matter.
- Reject organizer names and codes that appear only in the annotation, organization, structure, or scope-and-sequence explanations. The KG1, KG2, B1, B2, and B3 examples in the curriculum-reference diagram and sample table are explanatory examples, not target SFIs. Likewise, B4-B6 strand and sub-strand names in overview or scope-and-sequence tables summarize coverage and must not be extracted from those summary tables.
- Do not interpret the cover phrase "BASIC 4 - 6", a table-of-contents entry, a progression statement such as "B1 to B6", or a B4/B5/B6 column label as a Grade SFI. A Grade candidate requires a visible grade organizer in the detailed curriculum section, such as "BASIC 4", "BASIC 5", or "BASIC 6".

2. Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand organizers
- Accept a visible BASIC 4, BASIC 5, or BASIC 6 heading as a Grade SFI. Accept visible Strand and Sub-Strand headings in the detailed standards section as Standard Grouping SFIs.
- When a visible heading area contains Grade, Strand, and/or Sub-Strand labels together, return each organizer as a separate candidate in source order. Do not combine "Basic 4 / Strand 1 / Sub-strand 1" into one candidate.
- Preserve the complete visible organizer label as the description, including the hierarchy term, ordinal, punctuation, and topic. For example, "Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations" must remain exactly that full description; shortening it to "Variables and Equations" is a material error. Do not reduce a Strand or Sub-Strand candidate to only its ordinal, and do not create a candidate from the generic words "STRAND", "SUB-STRAND", "CONTENT STANDARD", or other table-column headers.
- Do not infer a missing organizer from a coded statement, a section path, a scope-and-sequence table, or expected hierarchy. The source contains missing, repeated, and inconsistent Sub-Strand headings and ordinals. Extract only organizers that are visible in the current raw block or table content.
- Treat repeated organizer names as source-scoped. The same Strand or Sub-Strand label can recur under different grades, and different visible Sub-Strand labels can share the same ordinal. Do not delete or rewrite a visible organizer merely because its ordinal or wording conflicts with another part of the document.

3. Content Standards and Indicators
- A normal Ghana Content Standard is the official statement in the left CONTENT STANDARD(S) column, usually paired with a four-component B4/B5/B6 code such as B4.1.1.1. A normal Indicator is the official learning-outcome statement in the INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS column, usually paired with a five-component code such as B4.1.1.1.1.
- Use source role, placement, and statement formatting together with the code. Do not classify every imperative sentence as an Indicator: exemplar activities are also imperative. Conversely, do not reject a concise imperative such as "Determine...", "Represent...", "Identify...", or "Create..." when it is the bold official coded indicator statement.
- A single table cell or row can contain more than one Content Standard and/or more than one Indicator. Split each separately bounded official code-and-statement pair into its own candidate. Do not combine neighboring standards because they share a row, cell, page, or source window.
- One official statement can wrap across lines or continue across adjacent raw rows. Preserve the complete statement as one candidate when the visible fragments clearly belong to the same code and statement. Do not split a statement at a line break, page break, mathematical expression, or column wrap.
- Do not truncate an Indicator at the first sentence when the bold official statement continues across lines. Do not append its E.g., Note, NB, Key Concept, diagram explanation, or teaching directions to the Indicator description.

4. Continuation pages and repeated material
- "CONT'D", "CONT’D", and equivalent continuation markers are page-layout labels, not part of an SFI description and not separate candidates.
- Repeated table headers and repeated column labels are not SFIs.
- A continued left-column Content Standard may be repeated across several pages or rows while new Indicators appear beside it. The repeated code and description still identify the same Content Standard. Within one validation result, group by canonical statement type, normalized code, and complete normalized description. Identical repeated occurrences must produce one source-grounded candidate with all contributing raw row/header indexes. Emitting separate candidates for those identical occurrences is a material error. Duplicate occurrences in different extraction windows may remain for downstream deduplication.
- A continuation row that contains only E.g. material, notes, diagrams, calculations, or activities does not create a new Indicator. Extract a new Indicator only when a new official indicator statement is visible. If the continued Content Standard is visible, it may still support the Content Standard candidate.
- If the same visible code is attached to materially different official descriptions, those are not continuation duplicates. Keep the distinct source statements as separate candidates and let later deduplication preserve the same-code/different-content evidence.

5. Material that is not an SFI
- Exclude all exemplars and example sequences beginning with "E.g.", including classroom tasks, worked examples, questions for learners, games, investigations, sample calculations, number charts, diagrams, illustrations, manipulatives, worksheets, and suggested teaching procedures.
- Exclude "Learners develop:" and all Subject Specific Practices and Core Competencies, including Problem Solving Skills, Critical Thinking, Justification of Ideas, Collaborative Learning, Attention to Precision, Cultural Identity, Global Citizenship, Personal Development and Leadership, and similar lists.
- Exclude Note, NB, Key Concept, reminders, cautions, cross-references, figure captions used as teaching guidance, and statements such as "Diagram is on the next page".
- Exclude mathematical facts, formulas, tables, chart labels, sample data, and image/figure descriptions unless the exact text is part of the official bold Content Standard or Indicator statement itself.
- A code mentioned inside an exemplar, note, cross-reference, diagram, or explanatory paragraph does not establish a new candidate. The code must visibly introduce the official source item in the appropriate source role.
- Do not create LearningComponents from the concepts, subskills, methods, examples, or activities contained inside a Content Standard or Indicator.

6. Ghana code anomalies and malformed source text
- Preserve genuine source anomalies; do not silently rewrite a code to make the hierarchy look regular. Use statement_code only when an exact valid code is visibly supported by the candidate's own source text and matches the configured code type.
- Spaces around periods, inconsistent spacing, and adjacent trailing punctuation can occur in otherwise clear codes. Use the deterministic code match's normalized value in statement_code and preserve its raw value in source_text; do not change any alphanumeric component. For example, "B5. 1.2.3.1 Determine basic division fact up to 81" requires statement_code="B5.1.2.3.1", and "B5.1. 4.1.3 Round decimals to the nearest tenth and hundredth" requires statement_code="B5.1.4.1.3". Leaving either code null is a material validation error.
- The Basic 4 Number Operations page visibly prints an extra leading "B" before "B4.1.2.1.1". Treat B4.1.2.1.1 as the intended Indicator code when that exact five-component code is visible, but do not include the stray standalone "B" in statement_code or the Indicator description.
- Some source items have a clear official Indicator role but a malformed code. Do not drop the learning outcome solely because its code is malformed, and do not reclassify it as a Content Standard solely from component count. When the role and official statement are clear but no valid exact Indicator code is visible, retain the Indicator candidate with statement_code=null and preserve the visible anomalous prefix in source_text when needed for evidence.
- In particular, the questionnaire statement printed as "B6.5.2.2 Design and administer a questionnaire..." appears in the Indicators and Exemplars column beside Content Standard B6.4.1.2. Treat the learning-outcome statement as an Indicator, but do not invent a fifth component or silently rewrite the visible code; use statement_code=null unless a valid exact indicator code is visible in the same source item.
- The probability statement printed as "P6.4.2.2.3 Explain that the experimental probability approaches..." is an official Indicator statement with a visibly anomalous P prefix. Do not change P to B. Extract the Indicator with statement_code=null unless an exact valid B-code is independently visible for that same statement.
- Glued forms such as a complete five-component code immediately followed by statement text must be separated when the full code is visibly recoverable from the candidate's own raw source. For example, "B5.2.3.1.3Create a problem for a given equation" must produce statement_code="B5.2.3.1.3", description="Create a problem for a given equation", and source_text preserving the complete visible code-and-statement text. Treat a null statement_code in this formatting-only case as a material validation error. Do not borrow a code from a neighboring statement, infer a missing digit, change a prefix, or repair an incorrect numeric component.
- Do not invent candidates for missing sequence numbers, and do not assume that Indicator or Content Standard numbering is complete or sequential.

7. Known same-code/different-content cases and editorial artifacts
- Do not treat an official code as globally unique identity during extraction validation. The source reuses some codes for different official statements.
- B4.1.3.1 is visibly attached to two different Content Standards: "Develop an understanding of equivalent and improper fractions" and "Demonstrate an understanding of strategies for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions (same denominator, or one being a multiple of the others)". Both are separate Content Standard candidates when visible. Do not merge them or choose one as the correction of the other.
- The red struck-through "12 x 12" printed beneath both B4.1.3.1 statements is deleted editorial residue and is not part of either Content Standard description or source evidence quote.
- B6.3.3.5 is visibly reused for both "Describe the position of objects in space using the cardinal points" and "Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection translation) on a 2D shape". B6.3.3.5.1 is likewise reused for two different Indicators. Preserve each distinct source-visible statement as a separate candidate; do not combine them because the codes match.
- More generally, when identical codes have materially different descriptions or different source locations, preserve each visible official statement separately. Same code is not a reason to delete, merge, paraphrase, or force descriptions to agree.
- B4.3.3.1 and B4.3.3.1.1 are used for an earlier perimeter Content Standard/Indicator and later for the independently printed Position/Transformation duplicate section. Preserve the perimeter items and the later Position/Transformation items as separate candidates. The later Position/Transformation occurrence must also remain separate during extraction from the independently printed B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 occurrence; only downstream deduplication may consolidate that exact duplicate family.
- B5.3.2.2 is visibly attached to two different Content Standards: "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape" and "Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes". Preserve them as separate candidates. Do not merge the transformation statement with the volume statement or with the Algebra Indicators that share its collision row.
- Ignore obvious deleted/struck-through editorial text and obvious neighboring-cell spillover that is not part of the official bold statement. Do not otherwise repair grammar, spelling, punctuation, mathematical notation, or source wording.

8. Description, source text, language, and citations
- description must contain the complete official source-visible wording of the Grade/Strand/Sub-Strand label, Content Standard, or Indicator. Remove only a separately represented item code; preserve organizer hierarchy terms, ordinals, punctuation, and separators. Do not include the table column header, CONT'D marker, examples, competencies, notes, or unrelated neighboring text unless that text is actually part of the official statement wording. Including the candidate's code at the beginning or end of description, or shortening a complete visible organizer label, is a material validation error that requires a corrected result.
- When statement_code is non-null, it must equal the applicable deterministic code match's normalized value, while source_text must visibly pair the corresponding exact raw code surface with the complete candidate description. Preserve source-visible spacing and immediate adjacency between the raw code and statement text. Do not use a code appearing elsewhere in the window.
- For a clearly official no-code candidate caused by a malformed source code, source_text may include the malformed visible prefix plus the complete official statement, while statement_code remains null.
- Preserve Ghanaian English wording, capitalization, spelling, grammar, punctuation, symbols, ranges, units, and mathematical notation as visible. Do not improve or modernize the wording and do not translate.
- For table candidates, cite only the raw header/body row indexes that visibly contribute to the candidate. Do not cite the Subject Specific Practices/Core Competencies column or exemplar-only rows as evidence for an official statement. Include every adjacent raw row genuinely needed to reconstruct a split statement, but do not add unrelated context rows.
- Do not quote canonical headers, filldown helper values, section_path text, or inferred hierarchy as candidate evidence.

9. Validation decision
- Set passed=true only when the draft has complete coverage of all visible target SFIs in the window, contains no non-SFI material, separates distinct official statements correctly, preserves complete source wording, assigns source roles correctly, and handles codes and citations according to these rules.
- When correcting, return a complete replacement result in source order. Renumber candidates after all additions, removals, splits, or reordering. Preserve a clearly official Content Standard or Indicator even when its code is anomalous; prefer statement_code=null over inventing or silently repairing a code.
- Use auxiliary candidates only for unusually ambiguous source-visible material that is genuinely likely to be mistaken for an SFI. Treat auxiliary records for routine exemplars, competencies, notes, front matter, repeated headers, and other clearly excluded material as a material validation error that requires correction.

10. Known Basic 4 duplicated Position/Transformation source occurrence
- The source independently prints the same Position/Transformation hierarchy and statements twice: Sub-strand 2 with B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 and later Sub-strand 3 with B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1.
- Extraction must preserve both independently printed occurrences as separate source candidates with their exact visible labels, codes, source text, and provenance. Do not rewrite the later codes, suppress the later occurrence, or combine the two physical occurrences during extraction validation.
- Logical consolidation and canonical-code selection for this exact duplicated family belong to downstream SFI deduplication under sfi_dedup_instructions.

11. Required semantic scope validation
- Every candidate must contain identity_scope_values and code_scope_values with the exact contracts below.
- Grade candidates require identity_scope_values={}.
- Strand candidates require exactly {"Grade": canonical Grade}.
- Sub-Strand, Content Standard, and Indicator candidates require exactly {"Grade": canonical Grade, "Strand": canonical Strand} in that configured order.
- Accepted Grade values are "BASIC 4", "BASIC 5", and "BASIC 6". Accepted Strand values are "Number", "Algebra", "Geometry and Measurement", and "Data". Correct aliases to their configured canonical values.
- code_scope_statement_types is empty, so code_scope_values must be {} for every candidate.
- Treat a missing, extra, misspelled, noncanonical, or structurally incorrect scope entry as a material error requiring a complete corrected result.
- Independently verify semantic scope for each candidate occurrence. Explicit hierarchy labels in the candidate's own visible source units are strongest, followed by explicit hierarchy labels in the current visible heading block. When a required dimension remains absent, use the nearest compatible heading in the bounded section context. Reject stale older Grade or Strand values when a nearer compatible value is available unless candidate-local visible source directly contradicts it.
- Do not approve a scope merely because its label appears inside the candidate statement, an exemplar, a competency list, another table column, or stale cumulative section-path history. Do not assign one shared Strand merely because different candidates occupy the same table row or window.
- In a combined heading block, use the current visible Strand for a Sub-Strand in that same block. In a standards table, interpret each candidate from its own source cell and source role before using neighboring parallel cells.
- Ghana codes contain genuine inconsistencies. Use code structure as supporting or contradictory evidence, not as permission to overwrite a clearly visible active Grade or Strand. When candidate-local source role, exact code evidence, wording, and table geometry jointly conflict with the nearest heading, treat the case as a source-layout conflict and apply the known document-specific rule rather than automatically copying the heading.
- For the editorial column collision containing Content Standard B5.3.2.2, "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape", beside Algebra Indicators B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3, require B5.3.2.2 to have Grade "BASIC 5" and Strand "Geometry and Measurement". Require B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3 to remain under Grade "BASIC 5" and Strand "Algebra". Same-row placement and the surrounding Algebra section are not valid reasons to give the transformation Content Standard an Algebra scope.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions:
Resolve Ghana Mathematics Basic 4-6 hasChild relationships conservatively. Use only finalized SFIs and the supplied parent_candidates. The normal direct hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Strand -> Sub-Strand -> Content Standard -> Indicator when the corresponding source-visible parent exists.

General direct-parent policy
- Grade SFIs attach to the StandardsFramework root.
- Strand SFIs attach to the correct Grade.
- Sub-Strand SFIs attach to the correct Strand within the correct Grade.
- Content Standards attach only to a source-supported Sub-Strand.
- Indicators attach only to a source-supported Content Standard.
- Choose exactly one direct parent unless unresolved=true. Do not substitute a broader ancestor or a same-type sibling merely to avoid unresolved.

Evidence policy
- Treat checker-approved identity scope, explicit current organizers, source-visible grouping/header relationships, and locally compatible configured code_parent_hint evidence as the strongest signals.
- Ghana codes are useful but not infallible. The source contains malformed prefixes, inconsistent numeric components, reused codes, and editorial collisions. A code_parent_hint is strong only when it is compatible with the candidate's local source context and is not contradicted by visible structural evidence or same-code/different-content audit evidence.
- Same table, same row, same segment, same window, active outline, nearest preceding grouping, nearby source context, and matched section-path labels are retrieval and ranking evidence. None of them alone proves a direct parent.
- A raw or malformed leading code-like prefix preserved in source_text is diagnostic evidence only. Do not treat textual dot-prefix structure as universally authoritative when no configured, locally compatible code_parent_hint exists.
- Do not infer a missing organizer or parent from an expected numeric sequence. Missing, repeated, and inconsistent Sub-Strand headings and code components are source facts, not permission to manufacture hierarchy.
- When code, table placement, active headings, or duplicate-code candidates conflict, select a parent only when the bounded evidence uniquely and coherently supports it. Otherwise return unresolved=true so the root fallback remains explicit and auditable.

Parallel-column and continuation behavior
- Ghana tables can place unrelated Content Standards and Indicators in the same extracted row or window. Do not attach an Indicator to a same-row Content Standard solely because of table proximity.
- Continued left-column Content Standards and row spans are strong local ranking evidence, especially for duplicate-code candidates, but require corroboration from the actual governed row/span, compatible scope, explicit grouping structure, or a locally compatible code-parent hint.
- For duplicate-code parent candidates, prefer the candidate supported by the child's exact source occurrence and governing continuation context. If the local evidence does not uniquely distinguish them, return unresolved rather than choosing by topical similarity.
- Same normalized code never authorizes one finalized parent to absorb another same-code source item. When multiple finalized candidates share a code, use the child's exact source occurrence, visible organizer, typed scope, and local row/span context to distinguish them. If those signals do not identify one direct parent, return unresolved=true.

Known canonicalized editorial exceptions
- For the merged Basic 4 fractions comparison/addition/subtraction Content Standard family, B4.1.3.2 is the canonical code. The preserved B4.1.3.1 occurrence is duplicate provenance, not a second hierarchy branch. Attach the finalized canonical item under the visible Basic 4 Number/Fractions hierarchy when that source-supported parent is supplied.
- For the merged Basic 4 Position/Transformation duplicate family, use the earlier Sub-strand 2 organizer and B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 canonical items. The later Sub-strand 3 and B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1 occurrences remain duplicate provenance and do not form a second logical branch.
- These exact exceptions do not authorize repairing, recoding, or reparenting other anomalous source items without equally specific source evidence.

Known Basic 4 B4.3.3.1 collision boundary:
- The earlier perimeter Content Standard/Indicator printed as B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1 remain distinct finalized items from the duplicated Position/Transformation family. Attach the perimeter items only to their source-supported perimeter/measurement organizer.
- The finalized Position/Transformation duplicate family uses the earlier Sub-strand 2 organizer and B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 canonical codes. Do not attach a child to the perimeter item merely because a later duplicate Position/Transformation occurrence reused B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1. If the bounded evidence cannot distinguish the same-code candidates, return unresolved=true.

Known B5.3.2.2 same-code/different-content boundary:
- The volume Content Standard "Demonstrate an understanding of volume of common 3D shapes" belongs under the source-supported Basic 5 Measurement Sub-Strand.
- The separate transformation Content Standard "Perform a single transformation (translation and reflection) of a 2D shape" must not be attached to Measurement merely because its printed code is B5.3.2.2. Select only a source-supported transformation/geometric organizer supplied in its parent candidates; otherwise return unresolved=true.
- Do not use the neighboring Algebra Indicators B5.2.3.1.2 and B5.2.3.1.3 as parentage evidence for the transformation Content Standard or vice versa.

Known Basic 5 Measurement organizer exception:
- The merged Basic 5 "Measurement" Sub-Strand represents the source-visible "Sub-Strand 2: Measurement" organizer. The earlier "Sub-strand 3: Measurement – Perimeter, Area, Capacity/Volume and Angle" occurrence is duplicate editorial provenance and must not form a second logical hierarchy branch.
- When the merged Measurement Sub-Strand is supplied as a parent candidate, attach the source-supported B5.3.2.x Content Standards whose visible content is measurement to that single organizer. Exclude the anomalous transformation Content Standard printed as B5.3.2.2; its parent must be resolved from its own source evidence or left unresolved. This exact exception does not authorize inventing or repairing other organizers.

Known Basic 5 omitted Number Operations organizer:
- In the detailed Basic 5 Number sequence, the source continues from the B5.1.1.x family directly into Content Standards B5.1.2.1 through B5.1.2.6, and the next visible Sub-Strand organizer is Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions. The source does not supply a visible Basic 5 Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations organizer for this sequence.
- Treat B5.1.2.1 through B5.1.2.6 as the intended Basic 5 Number Operations sequence for semantic interpretation, but do not invent or synthesize the missing Sub-Strand SFI during relationship resolution.
- When no finalized Basic 5 Number Operations Sub-Strand is supplied among parent_candidates, return unresolved=true with the StandardsFramework-root fallback for each B5.1.2.1-B5.1.2.6 Content Standard. Do not attach any of them to Sub-strand 1: Counting, Representation & Cardinality, Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions, a cross-grade Number Operations organizer, or another same-level sibling.
- Stale active-outline or section-path carry-forward, nearest-preceding grouping, Grade/Strand scope agreement, code sequence, or topical similarity does not make Counting or Fractions the direct parent. In particular, B5.1.2.6 must be resolved consistently with B5.1.2.1 through B5.1.2.5 when the true organizer is absent.
- Indicators in the B5.1.2.x sequence may still attach to their finalized B5.1.2.x Content Standard when local table/continuation evidence or a compatible code_parent_hint supports that direct relationship.

Known omitted-organizer families in the detailed Ghana tables:
- The detailed tables omit a visible immediate Sub-Strand organizer before several cleanly coded Content Standard families. Do not synthesize a missing organizer and do not treat the previously active Sub-Strand, a stale cumulative section-path label, or the only same-grade/same-strand candidate as the direct parent.
- Basic 4 Number: B4.1.4.1 is the decimal family implied by Sub-Strand 4, and B4.1.5.1 is the percent family implied by Sub-Strand 5. No finalized Basic 4 Number Sub-Strand 4 or Sub-Strand 5 organizer is supplied. When those organizers are absent from parent_candidates, return unresolved=true with the StandardsFramework-root fallback. Do not attach either Content Standard to Sub-Strand 3: Fractions, Counting, Number Operations, another sibling, or a cross-grade organizer.
- Basic 5 Number: B5.1.4.1 is the decimal-fractions family implied by Sub-Strand 4, and B5.1.5.1 is the percentage family implied by Sub-Strand 5. No finalized Basic 5 Number Sub-Strand 4 or Sub-Strand 5 organizer is supplied. When those organizers are absent from parent_candidates, return unresolved=true with the StandardsFramework-root fallback. Do not attach either Content Standard to Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions, Counting, a cross-grade organizer, or another sibling.
- Basic 6 Geometry and Measurement: B6.3.1.1 is the prisms family implied by Sub-Strand 1. Its source occurrence precedes the later visible heading Sub-Strand 3: Geometric Reasoning. Do not attach B6.3.1.1 to Geometric Reasoning merely because that is the only supplied Basic 6 Geometry-and-Measurement Sub-Strand, because it is nearby, or because Grade and Strand scope match. When no finalized Basic 6 Geometry-and-Measurement Sub-Strand 1 organizer is supplied, return unresolved=true with the StandardsFramework-root fallback.
- For all of these omitted-organizer families, code sequence may clarify why a supplied sibling is contradictory, but code alone does not authorize inventing the missing organizer. Indicators may still attach to their finalized Content Standard when local table/continuation evidence or a compatible code_parent_hint supports that direct relationship.

Structured scope interpretation for the current Ghana configuration
- The finalized identity-scope shapes are intentionally limited. Strand children carry Grade scope; Sub-Strand children carry Grade and Strand scope; Content Standard and Indicator children carry Grade and Strand scope.
- For Strand -> Grade and Sub-Strand -> Strand decisions, a complete structured-scope match is strong evidence because the child's configured scope directly names the expected parent value and the candidate's ancestor scope can also be compared.
- For Content Standard -> Sub-Strand and Indicator -> Content Standard decisions, direct_parent_value_match and scope_comparison.complete_match will normally be null/false because Sub-Strand and Content Standard are not configured identity-scope dimensions on those children. This absence is expected and is not evidence against a candidate and is not by itself a reason to return unresolved.
- For Content Standard and Indicator children, identity_scope_ancestor_match normally confirms only BASIC grade and Strand. It narrows the branch but does not identify the exact Sub-Strand or Content Standard parent. Resolve the exact parent from the child's source occurrence, explicit organizer/continuation context, table structure, locally compatible code-parent evidence, and the known Ghana exceptions below.
- A genuine finalized Grade or Strand scope conflict is strong evidence against a candidate, but source_local_controlled_parent_scope_conflict may arise from cumulative, stale, duplicated, or misnumbered source labels and must be reconciled with the complete bounded evidence rather than treated as an automatic rejection.

Additional Ghana code-parent anomaly rules
- B6.3.3.5/B6.3.3.5.1 is a same-code/different-content family. Keep the cardinal-position Content Standard and Indicator under their source-supported position organizer, and keep the reflection/transformation Content Standard and Indicator under their source-supported transformation/geometric organizer. Do not choose between these parent candidates by code alone.
- The decimal-section Indicator printed as B5.1.2.1.1 with the wording "Multiply multi-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers efficiently" is intentionally preserved as its own audited SFI. Its printed code points toward B5.1.2.1, its local placement points toward B5.1.4.1, and its wording resembles the separately printed B5.1.2.2.1 Indicator. None of those signals alone establishes a direct parent. Do not attach it to B5.1.2.1, B5.1.4.1, or B5.1.2.2 solely from code, row proximity, or semantic similarity. Return unresolved=true with the framework-root fallback unless one supplied parent candidate has explicit, coherent source evidence that resolves the contradiction. Do not treat unresolved as a reason to discard or rewrite the SFI.
- The volume/capacity Indicators printed as B5.3.3.2.2 and B5.3.3.2.4 occur under the source-visible B5.3.2.2 volume/capacity Content Standard. When the bounded evidence preserves that local governing structure, prefer B5.3.2.2 over the printed indicator prefix.
- The Indicators printed as B6.1.1.6.1 and B6.1.1.4.3 occur under the source-visible B6.1.2.6 Content Standard. When description and local continuation evidence agree, attach them to B6.1.2.6 rather than following the malformed prefix.
- The malformed B6.5.2.2 Indicator occurrence appears under B6.4.1.2, and P6.4.2.2.3 appears under B6.4.2.2. When the bounded source evidence supports those governing Content Standards, use the visible local parent rather than repairing or following the malformed printed prefix.
- These anomaly rules apply only to the exact source patterns described. They do not authorize generic code correction or topical reparenting elsewhere.
as.sfi_has_child_validation_instructions:
Audit Ghana Mathematics Basic 4-6 hasChild decisions independently and conservatively. Apply the producer instructions, but do not merely endorse the producer rationale. Re-evaluate the child against every supplied parent candidate and return a complete corrected response whenever the selected parent, root use, multiplicity, or unresolved state is materially wrong.

Required Ghana hierarchy and cardinality
- The intended direct hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Strand -> Sub-Strand -> Content Standard -> Indicator.
- A resolved Grade must have the StandardsFramework root as its sole direct parent.
- A resolved Strand must have exactly one Grade parent.
- A resolved Sub-Strand must have exactly one Strand parent in the correct Grade.
- A resolved Content Standard must have exactly one source-supported Sub-Strand parent.
- A resolved Indicator must have exactly one source-supported Content Standard parent.
- Ghana is not modeled as polyhierarchical. More than one selected parent for any resolved child is a material error. Correct it to one direct parent or set unresolved=true with no selected parents.
- The root must not be selected as the resolved parent of Strand, Sub-Strand, Content Standard, or Indicator. Root fallback is appropriate only for a top-level Grade or for an unresolved child.

Structured-scope audit policy
- Treat child and parent identity_scope_values as finalized structured evidence, not as infallible source truth. A Grade or Strand conflict is normally a material cross-scope error unless the bounded evidence clearly demonstrates that the finalized scope itself is anomalous.
- For Strand -> Grade and Sub-Strand -> Strand, direct_parent_value_match and complete_match are especially useful. A conflicting candidate should not be selected when a matching supplied candidate is source-supported.
- Under this Ghana configuration, Content Standard and Indicator children carry only Grade and Strand identity scope. Therefore direct_parent_value_match is normally unavailable for Content Standard -> Sub-Strand and Indicator -> Content Standard. Null direct-parent comparison or complete_match=false is expected at those levels and must not be treated as evidence of no parent.
- For Content Standard and Indicator children, identity_scope_ancestor_match only confirms the Grade/Strand branch. It does not distinguish the exact Sub-Strand or Content Standard among candidates in that branch.
- `source_local_controlled_parent_scope` and `source_local_controlled_parent_scope_conflict` come from typed bounded labels that may be cumulative, stale, duplicated, misnumbered, or emitted in unusual reading order. Use it as evidence, not an automatic decision. Prefer explicit current organizers, exact source occurrence, governing continuation/row-span structure, and coherent finalized scope.

Source and code audit policy
- Same row, same table, same segment, same window, active outline, nearest preceding grouping, nearby source order, and section-path matches are retrieval evidence only. A same-row parallel-column item or stale cumulative heading is not automatically the parent.
- A locally compatible configured code_parent_hint is strong evidence, but Ghana codes are not infallible. Reject code-only parent selection when the source-visible organizer, exact occurrence, continuation context, or same-code/different-content audit evidence supports another supplied parent.
- Do not infer missing hierarchy items from numeric sequence and do not repair codes. Choose only among supplied endpoints.
- For continuation rows, identify the Content Standard that actually governs the child's source row/span. Do not attach an Indicator to a neighboring Content Standard from a parallel column.
- Return unresolved=true only when the supplied evidence cannot defensibly identify one direct parent. Do not use unresolved merely because some weak evidence conflicts when one candidate is coherently supported by exact scope, source occurrence, organizer/continuation structure, or a locally compatible code hint.

Known Ghana exceptions that must be audited
- Basic 4 Fractions: the finalized comparison/addition/subtraction Content Standard family uses canonical B4.1.3.2. Its preserved B4.1.3.1 occurrence is duplicate provenance, not a second parent branch. Keep the distinct B4.1.3.1 equivalent/improper-fractions item separate.
- Basic 4 Position/Transformation: the later Sub-strand 3 and B4.3.3.1/B4.3.3.1.1 occurrence is duplicate provenance for the earlier Sub-strand 2 and B4.3.2.1/B4.3.2.1.1 family. Do not create or select a second logical branch from the duplicate occurrence.
- Basic 4 B4.3.3.1 collision: the earlier perimeter Content Standard/Indicator are distinct from the later Position/Transformation occurrence with the same code. Parent each by exact source content and organizer, not by the reused code.
- Basic 5 B5.3.2.2 collision: the volume Content Standard belongs under Measurement. The transformation Content Standard is distinct and must not be attached to Measurement merely because its code is also B5.3.2.2. The neighboring Algebra Indicators are not its parentage evidence.
- Basic 5 Measurement organizer: use the single finalized Measurement Sub-Strand represented by the source-visible Sub-Strand 2 organizer; the earlier misnumbered Measurement heading is duplicate editorial provenance, not a second branch. Exclude the anomalous transformation B5.3.2.2 item from that measurement rule.
- Basic 6 B6.3.3.5 collision: the cardinal-position and reflection/transformation Content Standards and their B6.3.3.5.1 Indicators are distinct same-code items. Select the parent matching the child's exact source occurrence and mathematical statement.
- Basic 5 omitted Number Operations organizer: the source-visible B5.1.2.1 through B5.1.2.6 Content Standards form the intended Basic 5 Number Operations sequence, but no finalized Basic 5 Number Operations Sub-Strand is available. Fail any producer response that resolves one of these Content Standards to Sub-strand 1: Counting, Representation & Cardinality, Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions, a cross-grade Number Operations organizer, or another sibling using stale outline/section-path evidence, nearest-preceding grouping, Grade/Strand scope alone, code sequence alone, or topical similarity. Accept and, when necessary, correct to unresolved=true with no selected parent and the framework-root fallback. Apply this consistently to B5.1.2.6 as well as B5.1.2.1 through B5.1.2.5. This exception does not prevent a locally supported B5.1.2.x Indicator from attaching to its finalized B5.1.2.x Content Standard.
- Other omitted Number organizers: fail any producer response that attaches B4.1.4.1 (decimals) or B4.1.5.1 (percent) to the Basic 4 Fractions, Counting, Number Operations, another sibling, or a cross-grade organizer when no finalized Basic 4 Number Sub-Strand 4 or 5 organizer is supplied. Likewise, fail any response that attaches B5.1.4.1 (decimal fractions) or B5.1.5.1 (percentage) to Basic 5 Fractions, Counting, another sibling, or a cross-grade organizer when no finalized Basic 5 Number Sub-Strand 4 or 5 organizer is supplied. Stale active-outline state, cumulative section-path labels, nearest-preceding grouping, Grade/Strand agreement, code sequence alone, and topical similarity do not establish those direct parents. Accept and, when necessary, correct each Content Standard to unresolved=true with no selected parent and the framework-root fallback. Their locally supported Indicators may still attach to the corresponding finalized Content Standard.
- Basic 6 omitted prisms organizer: B6.3.1.1 is the prisms Content Standard implied by Geometry-and-Measurement Sub-Strand 1, and its source occurrence precedes the later Sub-Strand 3: Geometric Reasoning heading. Fail a producer response that attaches B6.3.1.1 to Geometric Reasoning solely because it is the only supplied same-grade/same-strand Sub-Strand, appears nearby, or matches Grade and Strand scope. When no finalized Basic 6 Geometry-and-Measurement Sub-Strand 1 organizer is supplied, accept and, when necessary, correct to unresolved=true with no selected parent and the framework-root fallback. Locally supported B6.3.1.1.x Indicators may still attach to the finalized B6.3.1.1 Content Standard.
- Basic 5 anomalous decimal-section B5.1.2.1.1: this multiplication occurrence is intentionally preserved as a separate audited SFI. Its code, local decimal-section placement, and similarity to B5.1.2.2.1 conflict. Fail a producer response that chooses B5.1.2.1, B5.1.4.1, or B5.1.2.2 only from one of those signals. Accept unresolved=true with the framework-root fallback when no supplied candidate has explicit, coherent evidence resolving the contradiction. Do not correct the code, merge the item semantically, or require a speculative parent merely to avoid unresolved output.
- Basic 5 volume/capacity malformed prefixes: Indicators printed as B5.3.3.2.2 and B5.3.3.2.4 should follow the source-visible B5.3.2.2 volume/capacity Content Standard when the local evidence supports it.
- Basic 6 malformed prefixes: Indicators printed as B6.1.1.6.1 and B6.1.1.4.3 should follow B6.1.2.6 when the local source evidence supports that governing standard. The malformed B6.5.2.2 occurrence should follow B6.4.1.2, and P6.4.2.2.3 should follow B6.4.2.2, when those visible local parents are supplied and supported.

Verdict policy
- Set passed=true only when the producer selected the correct single direct parent, or correctly used unresolved because no supplied direct parent can be defended.
- Set passed=false for a wrong hierarchy level, cross-grade or cross-strand attachment, code-only selection contradicted by source structure, incorrect root use, unjustified unresolved decision, or multiple selected parents.
- When correcting, return a complete response for the request and use only supplied endpoint IDs. Explain the decisive source/scope evidence and any known Ghana anomaly applied.

lc.generation_instructions: Decompose each Ghana Mathematics Indicator SFI into atomic mathematical skills or concepts directly supported by the Indicator's own text. The leading code (e.g. B5.1.1.3.4) is an identifier, not content: never copy it into skill text and never derive grade, strand, or sub-strand scope from it - codes in this source contain visible errors. Many Indicators are already atomic (e.g. 'Round decimals to the nearest tenth'): emit exactly one clean skill for these and never pad the skill count. Compound Indicators split along their own structure: paired verbs ('read and write', 'compare and order', 'count and convert ... and vice versa', 'estimate and calculate') are usually two skills; clause chains ('identify the unknown, represent the problem with an equation, and solve the problem') split per clause. Keep parenthetical scope qualifiers ('up to 100,000', 'to the nearest tenth', '(cm, m)') attached to their skill - never drop them or spin them off as separate skills. If exemplar text leaked into the seed (starting 'E.g. 1.' or 'Ask learners to...'), ignore everything from that point: exemplars, subject-specific practices, and core competencies are activities, never skills; lowercase 'e.g.'/'i.e.' inside a statement is legitimate content, not an exemplar boundary. Preserve NaCCA terminology and British spelling exactly (factorisation, multi-base materials, referents, highest common factor (HCF), Ghana Cedis). Output skills in English.
